thread:
jess (support): Hey team, raising a customer escalation — Acme sees intermittent 401s when calling Redwood from a Vercel Edge function using our TS SDK v0.9.2. Happens only when they deploy with a service worker enabled.

sam (support): Oof. Got any logs or a repro?

jess (support): Their root request shows `401 Authorization failed` from our auth gateway. From the browser console: `Access to fetch at \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat\" from origin \"https://acme.app\" has been blocked by CORS policy` — but server logs show the 401 before CORS preflight returns.

ryan (devex): Can you paste their client code? Suspect header ordering or fetch options in edge runtime.

jess (support): They shared this minimal snippet from Vercel edge fn:

```ts
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
export default async (req) => {
  const res = await client.chat.completions.create({ model: 'gpt-4o-mini', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }] });
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(res));
};
```

lee (runtime-eng): Two things to check: 1) service worker can mutate or re-order `Authorization` header in some runtimes, 2) preflight + `credentials: 'include'` can cause signed cookies to be sent and break our auth handshake.

sam (support): They also reported duplicate billing spikes around the same time as retries. Could retries be re-sending on 401?

anya (billing): If client retries after a 401 without idempotency keys, each attempted token-exchange or request may bill. Need to confirm if retries originate client-side or via our SDK retry policy.

jess (support): Customer environment: Node 18 (edge runtime), Vercel platform, SDK @redwood/inference@0.9.2, they have a service-worker that proxies `fetch`. They tried both `fetch` in edge and a SSR route — edge only fails.

ryan (devex): We shipped a fix in 0.10.0 for header ordering in edge runtimes (re: Vercel service worker altering `Authorization`). Can they upgrade to 0.10.0 and test? That fixed a few internal repros.

jess (support): Asked them to try upgrade — they said they can't immediately because of monorepo constraints. Any quick patch we can recommend?

lee (runtime-eng): Short-term try: ensure the service worker doesn't call `event.respondWith`/`fetch` that mutates headers. Also try explicitly setting `Authorization` late: `const headers = new Headers(req.headers); headers.set('authorization', 'Bearer ' + process.env.REDWOOD_KEY);` and pass a raw `fetch` to our runtime (bypass service worker path).

ryan (devex): Also suggest disabling `credentials: 'include'` to avoid signed cookie preflight. Edge runtimes sometimes convert `Authorization` -> `authorization` and SWs reserialize.

jess (support): Sent quick repro instructions to customer. They said they still see CORS console error even after 0.10.0 in a canary test, but server logs show 401 -> then aborted preflight.

lee (runtime-eng): If server returns 401 during preflight handshake, upstream may be rejecting preflight due to missing or malformed `Origin`/`Host` headers from the edge function. Add temporary debugging to dump the incoming headers at our gateway for that request id.

ryan (devex): Action items: 1) ask customer to attempt v0.10.0 (or patch Authorization set workaround), 2) provide them a snippet to disable service-worker proxying for that route, 3) we will add enhanced request logging for the failing request id.

anya (billing): I'll monitor billing spikes for their org id (acme_org_42) between 2026-06-01 and 2026-06-03 and open a charge dispute if duplicate charges are confirmed.

jess (support): Customer provided failing request id: r-33a7f1b2. Lee, can you pull gateway headers for that id?

lee (runtime-eng): Pulling now.

deploy-bot: [deploy] New logging patch rolled to staging at 2026-06-04T12:04:00Z (rollout 20%).

lee (runtime-eng): Confirmed: request r-33a7f1b2 has `authorization` header present but value is truncated (only 'Bearer <partial token>'). Service worker in Vercel stripped cookies and clipped large headers on proxy path.

sam (support): So SW is mutating/truncating, producing 401, SDK retries -> duplicate requests -> billing spike.

ryan (devex): Recommend customer: (A) upgrade to SDK 0.10.0 which adds a header resend/fallback, (B) disable the service worker for the Redwood route, (C) temporarily add an idempotency key header for chat completions: `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` so retries are deduped on their side. Share example:

```ts
await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: 'gpt-4o-mini',
  messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'hi' }],
  headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': crypto.randomUUID() }
});
```
jess (support): Customer testing upgrade now. I'll follow up with results. :eyes:

anya (billing): If they show evidence of double charge caused by retries, billing will refund the duplicates. I'll need request ids + timestamps.

jess (support): Thanks all. I'll keep thread updated. Ticket #SUP-8277 linked to this thread.

ryan (devex): I'll draft a short KB for edge service-worker pitfalls (Authorization truncation, preflight credentials) so support can reuse.

lee (runtime-eng): And I'll add stricter validation to gateway that rejects truncated tokens earlier with a helpful error code (401E_TRUNCATED_TOKEN) so it's easier to diagnose in future.

jess (support): Closing loop once customer confirms.
